not_findings.description: Path to the decided non-issues list

attack.description: How to attack in this lens: the techniques that find what the criteria call wrong

blocker.description: What blocks in this lens: its dimension's definition of a blocker, set when the repository is calibrated. Reviewers and the Judge get it, and a finding the Judge shows meets it blocks

include_generated.description: This lens's reviewers get generated files in the diff too

generated.description: Generated files are left out of the diff a review sends, each listed with its line counts. Reviewers can still read them in the repository. Generated means by path: code generators' naming conventions, these paths, or the base's .gitattributes linguist-generated; never by a file's contents

exclude.description: Leave generated files out. Default true

paths.description: More paths that are generated, besides code generators' naming conventions

costs.description: What estimates are made from. A binding that sets its own prices in the user's config keeps them

prices.description: US dollars per million tokens, by model, or by binding name for a binding that names no model

cached_input_per_mtok.description: Input read from a cache. Left out, it costs what other input does

cache_write_per_mtok.description: Input written to a cache. Left out, it costs what other input does

per_call.description: Tokens each call by a role takes beyond the text ACR sends it and reads back: what its tools read, its turns, its thinking

stages.description: What every round does besides its lenses' reviewers. gate: first, before any reviewer, changed lines no test runs and breaks in changed code every test passes; a gap that blocks stops the round, sparing the reviewers until the tests are written. brief: before the reviewers, the Orchestrator writes each lens a brief for this change: where to attack, and how. context: every role gets what the repository's history says about the changed files. claims: a lens that checks every claim the change makes about itself. mutation: a lens that proposes small breaks in the changed code, which the pipeline runs against the tests; a break they miss is a finding. probes: a lens that writes and runs scenarios of what the change says it does, which needs a binding with a shell. test-writing: between rounds of a review to convergence, a fresh writer pins each fixed blocker with a test that fails before the fix and passes after, and closes the gate's gaps.

tests.description: How the repository's tests run, for the mutation stage.

command.description: Run from the repository's root. {tests} stands for the test files to run. Without it, it's found from the repository's files: Flutter, Cargo, Go, npm or pytest.

parallel.description: How many mutants run at once.

timeout.description: Seconds one run of the tests may take.

mutants.description: How many mutants a reviewer proposes in a round.

setup.description: Run once a round, from the root of a copy of the change, before any reviewer's copy is made from it: the package install and a first build, so every copy starts warm.

coverage.description: The command that runs the tests with coverage, from the root, writing an lcov report, for the gate.

report.description: Where the coverage report is, from the root: coverage/lcov.info if unset.

gate.description: What a gap that blocks does: stop the round before the reviewers (the default), or warn and let them run.

variants.description: Other ways the gate runs the change's own tests, each once, such as in random order, one at a time, or in another time zone.

command.description: From the root, with {tests} for the test files.

repeat.description: How many more times the gate runs the change's own tests plainly, after the first, to catch one that passes only sometimes.

runbook.description: How to work in this repository on this machine: setting up a copy, running its tests and probes, guarding a command that could hang, and where dependency and SDK sources are. Every role that can run things gets it.
